/SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Issued at 257 PM MDT Wed Sep 23 2026

Saturday morning, a weak 500-mb trough looks to be over the forecast 
region. Surface winds out of the northwest are possible with a weak 
cold front across Eastern Colorado. However, high temperatures are 
forecast to rise into the 80s across the forecast area despite the 
troughing overhead and weak cold front. This would likely be due to 
weaker surface winds alongside clearing of cloudcover, which would 
allow solar heating to dominate as the primary heating mechanism for 
the day. This solution is supported by LREF guidance, which shows a 
60% chance or higher for less than 10% cloudcover along and west of 
U.S. Highway 83. In addition, NBM guidance suggests a 50% chance or 
greater that surface winds will remain below 10 mph across most of 
the forecast region. Even NBM 25th percentile high temperatures are 
in the 80s across the CWA (County Warning Area) except along U.S. 
Highway 283 where lingering cloudcover may keep highs in the upper 
70s. It should be noted that forecast guidance indicates relative 
humidities dropping into the teens across portions of Eastern 
Colorado Saturday afternoon, which could indicate some potential for 
critical fire weather conditions. However, NBM guidance suggests a 1 
in 3 chance or less that wind gusts will exceed 25 mph across most 
of this area, which leaves confidence in fire weather conditions 
occurring less than 5%. 

Ridging looks to build into the forecast area Sunday, with ensemble 
guidance suggesting that this will transition into more 
southwesterly upper-level flow by Monday morning. Conditions 
continue to be forecast in the upper 70s to mid 80s across the 
forecast region. Precipitation remains unlikely at least through the 
morning hours on Monday, as NBM precipitation guidance remains below 
a 10% probability for all areas that greater than 0.1 inches of rain 
will occur. 

Troughing is forecast to begin moving overhead sometime Monday 
afternoon or evening. A surface low at the leading edge of this 
trough would be expected to deepen with the aid of sufficient upper-
level divergence and lee cyclogenesis across the Central and North-
Central Plains. A cold front appears likely as the surface low 
passes through the forecast area sometime between the afternoon and 
night hours Monday. Chances for precipitation increase dramatically 
along the frontal boundary, as NBM guidance shows that most areas 
have at least a 40% chance for greater than 0.1 inches of rain with 
this activity through 6 am Tuesday. Areas north and east of a line 
from Trenton, NE to Hill City, KS have as high as a 75% chance for 
the same. Some of this activity may be associated with 
thunderstorms, particularly along and east of U.S. Highway 83 where 
LREF guidance shows between a 1 in 2 and 1 in 3 chance that surface 
CAPE (a measure of atmospheric instability) will be above 1000 J/kg. 
The same guidance suggests between a 40 and 50% chance that sfc-
500mb wind shear will exceed 30 knots, which could allow some 
thunderstorms to become severe if they develop. High winds would be 
the biggest concern with these storms, as GFS and EC model soundings 
suggest the vertical wind shear would be along the cold front. 
Additionally, CAPE and wind shear seem like they would be a bit low 
for large hail and tornadoes to occur with storms. As such, a 
reasonable forecast would be widespread showers and thunderstorms 
along the cold front, with perhaps a storm or two having a chance to 
produce severe wind. Confidence in severe weather occurring Monday 
night and into Tuesday is around 5%. 

Forecast guidance becomes a lot more uncertain by Tuesday morning. 
Ensemble guidance is in support of troughing remaining overhead into 
the evening hours, but becoming less certain on how quickly the 
upper trough will move out of the forecast area. LREF guidance 
doesn't seem to favor the trough moving out of the area until 
Wednesday morning, when about 55-60% of the members show 500-mb 
heights above 576 dam (5760 meters). However, even by Wednesday 
afternoon, 30% of the members still show the trough in the area. 
Cooler temperatures seem likely Tuesday afternoon, with highs 
forecast in the upper 60s to mid 70s. However, conditions on 
Wednesday would depend on whether the trough is still in the area or 
not. If the feature has moved off to the east, warmer and drier 
conditions could be expected, with highs in the mid 70s to 80s. 
Otherwise, cooler and wetter conditions would be expected to remain 
in place.
